items.evidence: Skeleton-tier cross-check (consonantal_index.json) of Prov.15.1 against Prov.15.2 confirms zero shared skeleton tokens, matching the row's own substrate claim; the verb pair יָשִׁ֣יב/יַעֲלֶה carries the antithesis without needing an adversative particle for the classification to hold. items.claim: The antithesis argued for Prov.15.2 is substantively correct but is built entirely on transliteration, never a quoted Hebrew run.
items.evidence: Skeleton check confirms the named forms (לְשׁ֣וֹן חֲ֭כָמִים / תֵּיטִ֣יב // וּפִ֥י כְ֝סִילִ֗ים / יַבִּ֥יעַ) and the pi-kesilim...ivvelet template recurring at 15:7 and 15:14 (verse_map_oshb.json) are accurate, and the no-shared-token rejection of a 15:1 chain holds. But the row never quotes a single pointed Hebrew byte string for this lexical/grammatical claim -- per the OL brief, a Hebrew claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement, and the standing toolkit rule requires quoting the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim. This is an evidentiary gap, not a boundary error: the single_proverb decision and the rejection of a 15:1 chain both stand.

items.claim: The synthetic-parallelism and first-of-nine-YHWH-verses claims for Prov.15.3 both check out on re-sweep, but the row again argues Hebrew structure only in transliteration.

items.claim: The antithesis and Prov.15.32 cross-reference for Prov.15.5 are correct, but the row's transliteration 'evil' for the verse's actual subject is a homograph collision with the English word for wickedness that a quoted Hebrew run would have prevented.
items.evidence: The verse's opening word אֱוִ֗יל means 'fool,' not moral evil; rendering it as bare 'evil' in observed_substrate_signals ('subject pair evil / shomer tokhachat carries the antithesis') risks a reader taking the English sense of the transliteration rather than the Hebrew one. The discipline/reproof recurrence at Prov.15.32 is confirmed -- מ֭וּסָר and נַפְשׁ֑וֹ both reappear there -- and the eleven-verse gap claim is correct. The chapter's catchword-adjacency figure the row cites (7 of 32 pairs) matches prov_device_inventory.json exactly. This is the same transliteration-only 'insufficient engagement' gap as P07-002/003/007, elevated here because the specific transliteration chosen is actively misleading rather than merely unquoted.

items.claim: The proverb_cluster call for Prov.15.8-15.9 rests on a construct phrase that is an 11-verse book-wide macro-genre formula rather than a two-verse-only catchword, and the row's 'opens their second colon' framing misdescribes the etnahta-verified colon structure.
items.evidence: Both quoted Hebrew runs in the row (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה at 15:8; תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה at 15:9) collate to BYTE tier against their cited oshb refs -- no copy-degradation defect. But a skeleton-tier book-wide sweep of the phrase (sweep.py --skel) returns 11 verses, not 2: Prov.3.32, Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.15.9, Prov.15.26, Prov.16.5, Prov.17.15, Prov.20.10, Prov.20.23 -- a recurring 'X is toevat-YHWH' sentence-formula deployed independently across the book (Prov.11.1 and Prov.11.20 also close on the same 'his delight' word as Prov.15.8, with no adjacency between any of the other nine sites). The row's 'sweep: 2 consecutive verses' citation names the object correctly but omits the book-wide frequency, understating that the shared glue is a stock formula-class rather than a bespoke local catchword -- the C2 owner ruling treats a cluster whose only glue is a shared theme/formula as over-clustering. Separately, accent-codepoint verification (HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA falls on the word for YHWH in 15:8 but on the word for 'wicked' in 15:9) shows the phrase sits at the CLOSE of the pre-etnahta colon in 15:8 (after זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים) but at the OPEN of the pre-etnahta colon in 15:9 (before דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע) -- in neither verse does it fall in the post-etnahta second colon, so 'both lines open their second colon' does not hold at the byte/accent level; the two occurrences are not structurally parallel. The row does not address the shared 'wicked' root also touching Prov.15.6, an alternative local signal it leaves undisclosed. Recommend re-arguing as two single_proverb rows per the C2 default, or naming the formula-class explicitly and grounding cohesion in a genuinely local feature instead.
